newsitem.title: USA: Nike stock jumps on strong earnings.
newsitem.headline: Nike stock jumps on strong earnings.

text.p: The stock of Nike Inc. soared Thursday, a day after the company reported an 81 percent rise in second-quarter profits and soaring orders for its athletic apparel and footwear.
Several brokerages increased their earnings estimated for Nike, the world's largest footwear maker.
The stock rose $6.25 to $61.375 at mid-afternoon on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active issues.

Nike said Wednesday after the market closed that it earned $176.9 million, or 60 cents a share, in the three months ended Nov. 30. This far exceeded Wall Street's estimates and the year-earlier profit of $97.8 million, or 34 cents a share.
Sales jumped 55 percent in the quarter to $2.10 billion from $1.36 billion.

Hambrecht & Quist and Robertson, Stephens & Co. raised their earnings estimates for Nike for 1997 and 1998, after Nike said its "futures" orders for goods to be delivered from December through April surged 54 percent to $4.1 billion, compared with estimates generally in the 30 percent range.

Analysts said that even in the U.S. footwear market, which many consider to be mature, Nike sales rose 52 percent as the company continued to expand the market and take away share from rivals like Reebok International Ltd.
U.S. apparel sales rose 93 percent on top of a 100 percent increase in the same period last year.
International sales rose 64 percent, Nike said.

Nike President Tom Clarke predicted that within three years sales from abroad would represent more than half of the company's core athletic apparel and footwear business, up from about 40 percent currently.
Clarke said his recent discussions with retailers indicated the current holiday season would be a strong one.
The company reported order growth of more than 50 percent in key U.S. categories, including women's fitness, men's basketball, men's running and kids.
